messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with depressive disorder had decreased vitamin D levels compared with healthy controls.
Sentence: "The patients with DD had elevated TXB levels and decreased vitamin D levels, as compared to healthy controls."
Measured as: depressive disorder (vs healthy controls)
Population: Children and adolescents with depressive disorder and healthy controls
Intervention: Baseline vitamin D level (observational comparison)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 58
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D levels were not associated with a diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
Sentence: "Vitamin D levels were not associated with diagnoses of major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder."
Measured as: MINI diagnosis of major depressive disorder
Population: Pregnant women from Michigan at risk for depression (by EPDS score or history of depression)
Intervention: Maternal serum vitamin D level (observational, not assigned)
Comparator: Lower vs higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 117
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both findings bear on vitamin D level and depression diagnosis, but Study A shows lower vitamin D in depressed youth while Study B finds no association in at-risk pregnant women, so the populations differ most.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: children/adolescents with depressive disorder vs healthy controls, against pregnant women at risk for depression"}
